input: read ./prompt.md and follow the instructions there
errors: A stray `cat >> file` with no input blocked a foreground command until the 120 s timeout; stopped it and reran.

doc_friction.issue: alerts/<n>.md said to record a false positive only in the run record's notes, so the alert stayed at the head of the queue and every run re-triaged #1 (fixed in this PR with codeql-triage.json).
Step 0 says to work the queue 'until it is empty', but about 1,240 alerts are open and the head was all false positives. Taken literally, no run would reach routing.
The alert files say to push a claim branch security-fix/code-scanning-<n>, but the cloud harness allows pushes only to the session branch. The two instructions conflict.

deviations.why: Claiming needs a push to security-fix/code-scanning-<n>, which the harness forbids, and claim branches expire after 48h anyway.
deviations.did: Recorded the 11 verified false positives in a reviewed triage file that the queue honours, in place of claim branches and notes.
deviations.result: After merge, the next hourly queue run moves them to 'Triaged, awaiting dismissal', and the head of the queue becomes alerts that still need checking.

deviations.why: No new post: this is internal security tooling with no reader outside the repo.
deviations.did: Put the explanation in the module docstring, the triage file's _about and the PR body.

notes: False positives for the owner to dismiss (reasons in platform/security/codeql-triage.json): #1-#7 (py/clear-text-storage-sensitive-data), #95, #949, #950, #951. Not triaged and possibly real: #113/#114 photo-nutrition auth.mjs:45 compares a hand-chosen legacy client secret by unsalted SHA-256 (scrypt is used for new ones). Checked but not concluded: #952, #954, #1178, #1087/#1088 (print-atelier on main already uses randomUUID). Verification: cd platform/ci && python3 -m unittest test_security_alerts gave 19 OK; with the old security_alerts.py, 6 errors. control_plane_guard --check-coverage OK. risk_review: nothing blocked.

pricing.source: Anthropic pricing as cached in the Claude API skill (models table and per-model migration notes), 2026-10-06. Cache writes are 1.25x input (5-minute) and 2x input (1-hour); cache reads differ by model.

certainty.tokens: high: summed from the per-request `usage` the API returned, as the transcript recorded it, deduplicated by message id
certainty.model: high: the `model` field on each API response, not the configured model
certainty.api_equivalent_usd: medium: measured tokens x list prices in prompts/pricing.json (as_of stated); an equivalent, not a charge: these runs are billed under a subscription
certainty.time: medium: from transcript timestamps; model time is request-to-response, tool time is call-to-result, time waiting on a person is excluded from active time
certainty.human_equivalent: low: the agent's own estimate of how long a competent person would take, with its basis written down; never measured

not_counted: requests the harness makes outside the transcript (context compaction summaries, title generation, safety classifiers), if any
transcripts lost when a cloud session moved to a new container: only files present in this container are read, so a resumed session can undercount
server-tool fees (web search is billed per search, not per token); the count is recorded, not priced
CI minutes and the reviewer bots' own model calls
